passage:
"Jamal, stand up and show everyone your sums," said Mr Bilal, holding up the page covered in red crosses.
Jamal walked to the front. His face went hot and his eyes stung. He stared at the carpet while the whole class watched.
At dinner he pushed his rice around the plate.
"What is wrong?" asked Mum.
"The teacher showed my mistakes to everybody."
Mum put down her spoon. "That is not your fault, and I am glad you told me. I will talk to the school so that children can make mistakes and feel safe."
Jamal leaned against her arm.

qa.q: What did the teacher hold up in front of the class?
qa.a: He held up Jamal's page covered in red crosses.

qa.q: How did Jamal feel while standing at the front?
qa.a: He felt hot and wanted to cry, since his face went hot, his eyes stung, and he stared at the carpet.
She can talk to the school as she promised, so children can make mistakes safely, and keep listening to Jamal.

qa.q: How might Jamal's classmates have felt watching?
qa.a: Some may have felt uncomfortable or afraid that they would be next, since a child was shown up in front of everyone.

grounding: A teacher makes a child show his mistake to the class; he feels hot and wants to cry, tells his parent, and is told it is not his fault.

passage:
Monday. Karthik Sir held up Chandrika's page. "Look, she wrote her C backwards. Stand up, Chandrika, show everyone." She stood, face burning, eyes filling, while the class stared.
Tuesday. Chandrika would not put on her shoes. "I don't want school," she told Amma, and then all of Monday came out in sobs. Amma held her close. "It is not your fault. Mistakes are how we learn letters." That afternoon Amma went to talk with the head teacher.
Friday. Chandrika wrote a backwards C again. Karthik Sir knelt by her desk and quietly drew it the right way with her. She kept writing.

qa.q: What mistake did Chandrika make on her page?
What was Chandrika feeling when she had to stand in front of the class?
qa.a: She felt humiliated and close to tears: her face was burning and her eyes were filling while everyone stared.

qa.q: What did Amma do that helped?
qa.a: Amma listened, told Chandrika the mistake was not her fault, and went to talk with the head teacher that afternoon.

qa.q: How is Friday different for Chandrika from Monday?
qa.a: On Friday Karthik Sir helps her quietly at her desk instead of showing her mistake to the class, so she feels safe enough to keep writing.

grounding: A teacher makes a young child stand and show her mistake; she tells her parent, who says it is not her fault and speaks to the school, and later the teacher corrects her gently.

passage:
"Arnab, bring your spelling sheet up here," said Vidya Ma'am. She pointed at each red cross while the class watched. Arnab's neck went hot. He blinked hard so he would not cry.
At home, Mama was working late, and Arnab sat by the window with his sheet folded small in his pocket. He did not want dinner.
When the door opened at nine, he ran to her and it all spilled out.
Mama hugged him tight. "It is not your fault. Getting words wrong is how you learn them." Next morning she went with him to school and asked to see the head teacher.

qa.q: What was Arnab carrying in his pocket while he waited?
Why did Arnab blink hard at the front of the class?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and close to tears while Vidya Ma'am pointed at his red crosses, and he was trying not to cry in front of everyone.

qa.q: What could a school do so children like Arnab feel safe making mistakes?
qa.a: Teachers could go over mistakes privately and kindly, and the head teacher can listen when a parent raises a worry like Mama did.

qa.q: How might Mama feel when Arnab tells her what happened?
qa.a: She may feel protective and sad for him, which is why she hugs him, tells him it is not his fault and goes to the school the next morning.

grounding: A teacher shames a young child by showing his mistakes; with his parent working late he holds it in, then tells her, and she reassures him and goes to the school.
